title: Graph comparison for open then etale composition
statement: For a finite commutative ring A, a quasi-compact open immersion j:X to W and a separated quasi-compact etale map b:W to Z of Noetherian schemes, let r=j b with specified equality and e a compactification of r. The chosen open comparison [def-pur-graph-chosen-open-comparison], followed by the chosen graph comparison for b [def-pur-graph-chosen-etale-comparison] and the composite-adjunction sum/open compositor, equals the compact-support compositor, congruence to r, inverse t_e and the graph comparison for e [lem-asd-compact-support-graph-derived-isomorphism]. No proper Cartesian square is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0F7B (proper/quasi-finite interchange), 0F7F (change of base), 0F7I and 0F7J (composition); proper/open tower in parent steps 1–3. Graph normalization: etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0F4L.

proof.text: Apply the proved graph comparison for the identity-proper compactification of the open immersion. Its sheaf normalization and exact-derived identity-removal calculation are isolated in a proved module so each file remains within the compile limit.

Use compactification comparison coherence and the comparison-refinement equality to transport the preceding identity from the identity-proper compactification to the chosen compactification. This identifies graphChosenOpenComparison with graphChosenEtaleComparison for the open immersion.

Apply the proved identification of the open and etale derived adjunctions. The specified sum-composition counit theorem then identifies the conjugate inverse-image compositor in the conclusion with derivedEtaleSumCompIso.

Apply the existing support/sum compositor equation at the chosen input compactifications and the supplied output compactification. The global compositor transport formula identifies its support compositor with unboundedEtaleLowerShriekCompIso followed by the inverse output comparison. Cancel the identity comparisons of the two chosen compactifications, use naturality to put the graph comparisons in the displayed whiskering order, and substitute the preceding two identifications. Eliminate hr to restore the stated composite morphism.

lean.statement:
theorem graph_open_etale_composition
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {X W Z : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian W] [IsNoetherian Z]
    (j : X ⟶ W) [IsOpenImmersion j] [QuasiCompact j]
    (b : W ⟶ Z) [Etale b] [IsSeparated b] [QuasiCompact b]
    (r : X ⟶ Z) [Etale r] [IsSeparated r] [QuasiCompact r]
    (hr : r = j ≫ b)
    [HasCompactification j] [HasCompactification b] [HasCompactification r]
    [HasCompactification (j ≫ b)] (e : Compactification r) :
    let s := (conjugateIsoEquiv
      (derivedEtaleLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) r inferInstance)
      ((derivedOpenImmersionLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j).comp
        (derivedEtaleLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) b inferInstance))).symm
      (Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso
        (upperStarComp (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j b r hr) ≪≫
        Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso _ _)
    Functor.isoWhiskerRight (graphChosenOpenComparison A j)
        (rightDerivedLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) b) ≪≫
      Functor.isoWhiskerLeft
        (openImmersionLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j).mapDerivedCategory
        (graphChosenEtaleComparison A b) ≪≫ s =
      unboundedEtaleLowerShriekCompIso A j b ≪≫
        unboundedEtaleLowerShriekCongr A hr.symm ≪≫
        (rightDerivedLowerShriekIso A e).symm ≪≫
        canonicalEtaleCompactSupportComparison A r e
